commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to select a patient by index
commitResults.messageBody:
Caregivers need a way to pick one patient and see their full record,
but there is no command to select a patient from the list.

Let's add `view INDEX`, which follows the same index rules and
invalid-index message as `delete` so the two commands behave
consistently. For now it only reports which patient was selected;
showing the details comes in later changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track the viewed patient in the model
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel needs to know which patient to show, and must stay
correct when that patient is edited or deleted by another command.

Let's store the viewed patient in the Model as an observable value
that the view command sets and the UI can listen to.

ModelManager updates it when the address book changes:
* setPatient swaps in the new copy, e.g. after care info is added
* deletePatient clears it when the viewed patient is deleted
* setAddressBook clears it when the patient is no longer present,
  e.g. after clear

commitResults.messageTitle: Add backup command to save a copy of the data
commitResults.messageBody:
Users have no built-in way to keep a copy of their patient data before
risky changes, such as editing the data file by hand.

Let's add a backup command that saves all patient data to
data/backups/mediconnect-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json. The folder is created if
missing, a second backup in the same second gets a -1, -2 suffix instead
of overwriting, and a failed write reports the reason without touching
the data. The clock and folder can be passed in so tests can fix both.

Fixes #132

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover more backup cases in tests and docs
commitResults.messageBody:
BackupCommandTest did not check that a backup leaves the model and
viewed patient unchanged, that the file name follows the clock's time
zone, or that the default constructor uses the system clock and
data/backups. The overridden methods in BackupCommand also had no
header comments.

Let's add tests for these cases, give each test a single behaviour,
and add JavaDoc to execute, equals and toString. The UG now lists
backup among the commands that ignore extra parameters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain why a backup failed and tidy its path
commitResults.messageBody:
When the backup folder was read-only, the error only repeated the file
path, because Java's AccessDeniedException uses the path as its
message. A relative backup folder also produced paths such as
tp/../../var in the result. Users could not tell what went wrong or
where the file went.

Let's name the folder in the error and give a readable reason for
permission and other file system errors, and normalize the paths shown
to the user. The UG now warns against running backup after the data
file failed to load, since the next command replaces that file.

New tests cover a read-only folder, a relative folder, filtered lists,
special characters, non-English locales and every failure reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop trailing full stops from backup failure reasons
commitResults.messageBody:
Windows error reasons end with a full stop, such as "The directory name
is invalid.", so a failed backup showed "invalid.. Your data has not
been changed." Blank reasons were also shown as-is, leaving an empty
gap in the message.

Let's trim trailing full stops and spaces from the reason, and fall
back to the generic reason when nothing is left. The test for a folder
that cannot be created now checks the reason itself instead of looking
for "null" anywhere in the message, which failed whenever the temporary
folder's path contained "null".

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy backup command code and tests
commitResults.messageBody:
BackupCommand had an unused MESSAGE_USAGE, which the other commands
without parameters do not define, and its two-argument constructor had
no @param tags. Its timestamp formatter took the default locale when
the class loaded, so the test that changed the locale later could not
affect it and checked nothing.

Let's remove the unused constant, document the constructor and the
less obvious constants, and build the formatter with Locale.ROOT so
file names do not depend on language settings. File names were
already ASCII in every locale tried, so behaviour is unchanged. The
misleading locale test goes, and the test comments now share one style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn against typing exit after a failed data load
commitResults.messageBody:
The backup caution told users to "close MediConnect" before copying an
unreadable data file. Typing exit counts as a command, so MediConnect
saves its empty data over the file, which is exactly what the caution
is meant to prevent. Closing the window or using File > Exit does not
save patient data.

Let's say not to run any command, not even exit, and name the two safe
ways to close MediConnect.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test relative and default backup folders
commitResults.messageBody:
Two planted bugs went unnoticed by BackupCommandTest: dropping
normalize() from the error message, and changing the default folder,
as the test compared it with the constant itself. The UG and help text
promise data/backups, which restore will also rely on.

Let's test an error with a relative backup folder and check the
default folder against data/backups directly. The setup shared by the
relative folder tests moves into a helper.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop null data files from crashing MediConnect
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file holding only null, or a patient list with a null entry,
made MediConnect quit at startup with a NullPointerException instead
of starting with no patients as the UG says. JsonUtil.readJsonFile
passed Jackson's null result to Optional.of, and
JsonSerializableAddressBook.toModelType called toModelType() on the
null entry. A preferences file holding null had the same effect.

Let's report both cases as a DataLoadingException, which MainApp
already handles for other files that cannot be loaded.

Fixes #152

BackupCommandTest kept relativeToWorkingDir as a private helper, but
the restore tests need the same relative folder paths.

Let's move it into TestUtil so that both test classes share one copy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split saving a backup out of BackupCommand.execute
commitResults.messageBody:
Restore needs to back up the current data before replacing it, and
must report where that backup went. BackupCommand.execute only gave
the path inside its success message.

Let's move the saving step into saveBackup, which returns the path of
the new file. execute calls it, so backup behaves as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add restore command to load a backup file
commitResults.messageBody:
Users could save backups, but had no way to bring one back short of
replacing the data file by hand.

Let's add restore FILENAME, which loads a file from data/backups. It
checks the whole file first and backs up the current data before
replacing it, so nothing changes if either step fails. Missing,
unreadable and invalid files each get their own message. The file name
must not contain a folder, so it cannot point outside data/backups.

Fixes #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the assert that rechecks the backup name
commitResults.messageBody:
getBackupFilePath asserted that the chosen file does not exist, right
after a loop that only ends when it does not. The assert added nothing,
and it checked the file system, which another program can change at
any time, rather than a condition that only our code can break. Codecov
also counted it as a partially covered line.

Let's remove it. The suffix loop and its tests still make sure that no
backup is overwritten.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move the write failure reason into Messages
commitResults.messageBody:
BackupCommand had describeFailure, which turns a failed file write
into a short reason for the user. Restore already borrowed it, and
export needs it too, so it no longer belongs to one command.

Let's move it into Messages as describeWriteFailure, with its reason
constants and tests, and have backup and restore call it from there.

Export needs a patient's details and care lists as text, worded the
same as the detail panel, without a second copy of that formatting.

Let's add PatientFormatter, which formats the basic details, numbered
care entries with "None recorded" for empty lists, and the full
record. A line break inside an entry, which only a hand-edited data
file can hold, becomes a space, so each entry stays on one numbered
line. Export will use it, and the panel can switch to it once the
model PRs have numbered its lists.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add export command to save a patient's record
commitResults.messageBody:
Caregivers sometimes need a patient's details in a file, to print or
to send to a doctor, but MediConnect only showed them on screen.

Let's add export INDEX, which writes the patient's full record to
data/exports/NRIC.txt using PatientFormatter, starting with the date
and time of the export. Exporting a patient again replaces their file,
and a failed write gives the reason from Messages.describeWriteFailure.

Fixes #134

data backed up before anything is replaced, and the design choices
behind that. The empty archiving section goes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the separator for same-second backups

Let's name it SUFFIX_SEPARATOR, like the other parts of the name.

while the DG calls it automaticBackupFile, and MESSAGE_NO_PERMISSION

Let's move the result into createSuccessResult, rename the variable
and the constant to automaticBackupFile and MESSAGE_NO_READ_PERMISSION,
and give the failure reason in backUpCurrentData its own variable, as
the other commands do.

The line break sat inside String.format, so the next line mixed its
arguments with ioe, the second argument of the CommandException. The
coding standard prefers line breaks at a higher level. Backup and
restore break before String.format, but that line would pass 120
characters here, so the message is built first.

The detail panel tests started with an event such as

MalformedInputException instead. JsonUtil already turns that into a

shows its warning, and restore says the backup could not be read and
changes nothing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reserve each backup's name so that no backup is overwritten
commitResults.messageBody:
BackupCommand checked with Files.exists that a backup name was free,
and only later moved the written file there with REPLACE_EXISTING.
Two backups made at the same moment, e.g. in two MediConnect windows,
or a backup and the automatic backup of restore or clear confirm,
could take the same name, and one silently replaced the other.

BackupCommand now takes a name by creating an empty file there with
Files.createFile, which fails if the name is taken, and then tries
the next suffix. The written temporary file replaces that empty file,
which is deleted if the backup fails. On Windows, a folder with the
name gives AccessDeniedException rather than FileAlreadyExists-
Exception, so that also counts as taken when something has the name.

Fixes #368

which only a hand-edited data file can hold, showed in the panel as a
second line beside one number, e.g. "1. Penicillin" then
"2. Shellfish", which looked like a second entry. Exported records
already joined the lines with spaces, but the panel did not.

PatientFormatter#toSingleLine now does this for both: formatEntries
uses it as before, and the panel now uses it for every entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat a backup name as taken whenever something has it
commitResults.messageBody:
The check for a folder that Windows reports as access denied was a
branch that only Windows reaches, so the coverage from the Linux build
always missed it. Both exceptions now go through the same check: the
name is taken if something has it, and a free name with denied access
is still reported. Every path now runs on every operating system, and
the behavior is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Lock the backup folder instead of reserving a backup's name
commitResults.messageBody:
Reserving a name with an empty file, then replacing that file with the
written backup, failed on Windows CI: with many backups at once, one
got AccessDeniedException. On Windows, a file that is being replaced
is briefly pending deletion, and creating or checking a file of that
name then reports access denied rather than that the name is taken,
which cannot be told apart from a folder MediConnect may not write to.

Backups now take turns instead. A backup chooses its name, as before,
and saves the backup while it holds a FileLock on .backup.lock in the
backup folder, which makes backups in other processes wait. A process
can hold that lock only once, so the backups of one MediConnect also
take turns through a synchronized block. The backup is then written
as before, onto a name that no file has, so nothing is replaced, and
every path runs on every operating system.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat Unicode whitespace in medications as space
commitResults.messageBody:
A no-break space, often copied in from a web page or a chat app, is
not treated as whitespace by String#isBlank or by \s. A medication
that consists of a no-break space is accepted as a description, and
Aspirin 100mg with a no-break space is not the same medication as
Aspirin 100mg with a space. This is reported in #328.

Let's use (?U)\s, as for care entries, to check, normalize and
compare medication descriptions. Medication#normalizeDescription
holds the rule, and AddCareCommandParser calls it for the blank and
length checks. Without that change, addcare would pass a no-break
space to Medication and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

AddCareCommandParser belongs to another member. It changes only the
medication checks, which the care-entry change in #330 did not cover.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document spacing rules for medication entries
commitResults.messageBody:

web page, counts as a normal space. The duplicate rule of editmed

ignored. The duplicate rule of addcare already names the forms that
are ignored.

Let's say in the Field formats section that any kind of space is
treated as a normal space, and call the duplicate rule of editmed

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject addcare duplicates with no-break spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
The command addcare compares a new medication with the existing ones
after replacing runs of ASCII whitespace only. Aspirin with a
no-break space is not found to be the same as Aspirin 100mg with a
space. The command adds it, and Medication then turns the no-break
space into a space, so the patient has the same medication twice.

Let's use Medication#normalizeDescription, which treats Unicode
whitespace as whitespace, for the length and duplicate checks, and
remove the private copy of the rule in AddCareCommand.

This completes step 5 of #328 for medications. The file belongs to
another member and only the medication normalizer changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat equivalent Unicode forms of a medication as one
commitResults.messageBody:
Master treats an allergen or a care instruction that is written with
a letter and a combining accent as the same as one with the single
accented character, and the User Guide says so for addcare. A
medication is not: Medication is only trimmed and its whitespace
collapsed. So editmed accepts a description that looks the same as
another medication of the patient, and addcare adds it again.

Let's make Medication#normalizeDescription use the normalization of
the care entries, Patient#normalizeCareEntry, so that a description
is stored in Unicode form NFC. Medication#isSameMedication, which
editmed and the data file use, and the checks of addcare then find
that two descriptions that look the same are the same.

The User Guide gives the duplicate rule of editmed in the words of
the addcare rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move the normalization of entries to StringUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
Medication#normalizeDescription calls Patient#normalizeCareEntry, so
that a medication and a care entry are normalized in the same way.
This makes Medication depend on Patient, while Patient already
depends on Medication.

Let's put the normalization, Unicode whitespace collapsed and trimmed,
and Unicode form NFC, in StringUtil#normalizeEntry, a helper that
does not belong to the model. Both Medication#normalizeDescription and
Patient#normalizeCareEntry call it. Patient#normalizeCareEntry stays,
as a one-line call, so its callers do not change.

The behaviour is the same. StringUtil#normalizeEntry has its own
tests, and the tests of the medications and the care entries pass as
they were.

any word.

Mary-Jane and s/o, or end a word, as in Jr.

in two ways, and find O'Brien would not find O’Brien.

Let's replace curly apostrophes with straight ones when parsing a
name, and mention this in the User Guide.

0001-01-01 only gets the past-date note, and one such as 2207-11-05, a
typo for 2027, gets no note and stays listed as upcoming. A date of
birth before 1900-01-01 is already rejected.

data file and the Appointment constructor, and add a note when the
date is more than 2 years ahead. The far date is still added, as a
past date is, since it can be a real appointment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save only changed data and undo failed saves
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager saves the patient data after every command, and only
after the command has changed the Model. If the save fails, the
command is reported as failed, but its change stays on screen and is
lost on restart, or saved by a later command. If the data file is
read-only, even list, view, help and exit fail, so the app cannot be
closed with exit.

Let's take a Model.Snapshot of the patient data, list filter and
viewed patient before each command, save only if the patient data
changed, and restore the snapshot if the save fails. The error now
ends with "Nothing was changed." MainAppTest now expects list to leave
an unreadable data file as it is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save JSON files through a temporary file
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonUtil#saveJsonFile writes straight to the live file, so a save cut
off partway, e.g. by a full disk or a crash, can replace the last
valid patient data with a partial file, and the next launch starts
with no patients. Backups and exports already avoid this with
FileUtil#writeThroughTemporaryFile.

Let's save the patient data and the preferences through that method,
and have JsonAddressBookStorage create only the data folder, not an
empty data file, before the first save. FileUtil#createIfMissing is
then unused, so it is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix name, phone, address and NRIC validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Names with accented or non-English letters, such as Zoë, are
rejected, while s/o alone or at either end of a name is accepted.
Phones written with a space or hyphen, such as 9123 4567, are
rejected. An address of only Unicode spaces, such as an em space, is
accepted although addresses cannot be blank. A lowercase NRIC ending
in i is stored with a Turkish dotted I in a Turkish locale, which
makes the saved data unloadable.

Let's accept letters and accents in any language in names, reject
s/o, d/o, c/o, a/l and a/p at either end, remove spaces and hyphens
from phones before checking them, trim and reject Unicode whitespace
in addresses, and upper-case NRICs with Locale.ROOT.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden appointments against bad data and locales
commitResults.messageBody:
editappt and cancelappt format the appointment number with the
default locale, so in Arabic or Myanmar the message shows a digit such
as ٢ while the panel shows 2. A data file or backup can hold the same
appointment twice, although addappt and editappt reject it. Some
appointment code also assumes things it does not check.

Let's format both messages with Locale.ROOT, reject duplicate
appointments in the Patient constructor, as duplicate contacts are, so
such a file does not load, and add assertions and requireNonNull where
the appointment code relies on its callers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep w/o and other slash words as text in appointments
commitResults.messageBody:
In editappt, a note such as "MRI w/o contrast" changes who the
appointment is with to "o contrast", because w/o starts with the w/
prefix. addappt rejects the same note as a second w/. Notes cannot
hold c/o either, although names can.

Let's keep standalone s/o, d/o, c/o, a/l, a/p and w/o as text in
addappt and editappt, through the ignored slash words that
ArgumentTokenizer#tokenize now takes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the editappt assertion and drop an untestable one
commitResults.messageBody:

defines medical conditions and medical notes, which MediConnect cannot
record, and its heading, Acknowledgements and code links still refer to
AB3. The README does not say that the project is based on AB3, and my
AboutUs responsibilities are a placeholder.

editappt, cancelappt and listappt, define APPT_INDEX instead of the two
unsupported terms, name the DG after MediConnect, point its code links
to our repo, acknowledge AB3 in the DG and README, and give my real
responsibilities in AboutUs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the data file when a save fails
commitResults.messageBody:
Since #316, the data is written to a temporary file that then replaces
the data file. When the replacement fails, the error message shows the
exception's message, which names the temporary file, e.g. "Could not
save data to file ...\mediconnect.json.1490...tmp -> ...".

Let's name the data file itself when MediConnect may not write to it,
and for other failures give the short reason from
Messages#describeWriteFailure, as backup and export do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject misspelled and repeated data properties
commitResults.messageBody:
Patient data is read with unknown JSON properties ignored, and with the
last value kept when a property is repeated. A typo such as
"careInstructons", or a property given twice, therefore loads without
a warning, and the next save drops its values for good. Separately,
a save replaces the data file with a temporary file, which on macOS
and Linux succeeds even when the data file is read-only.

Let's read patient data and backups with a strict mapper that rejects
unknown and repeated properties, naming an unknown one as invalid
data, while preferences stay lenient. Let's also have
FileUtil#writeThroughTemporaryFile refuse to replace a file that
cannot be written to, as export already does.

An appointment's WITH and note can hold a line break when the data
file is edited by hand, and listappt then shows the rest as a fake
second appointment. Neither has a length limit. A no-break space, often
copied from a web page, is not treated as a space, so WITH can look
blank, and "Dr<no-break space>Tan" is not a duplicate of "Dr Tan".

Let's require WITH and the note each to be one line, of at most 100
and 500 characters, in commands, the model and the data file, and treat
Unicode whitespace as whitespace when trimming WITH and the note and
when comparing WITH for duplicates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say listappt lists active patients in the UG

appointments of all patients. The next bullet, the usage message and the
code all skip archived patients, so the summary contradicts them.

Let's say "all active patients" in the summary, as the rest of the
section does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject appointments before the date of birth
commitResults.messageBody:
An appointment can be dated before the patient was born, e.g.
addappt 1 d/1900-01-01 for a patient born in 1948, and edit dob/ can
move the date of birth past existing appointments. Such a record is
impossible, but it is saved, exported and loaded as if it were valid.

Let's make Patient reject appointments before its date of birth, so a
data file or backup holding one counts as invalid data. Let's also
check it in addappt, editappt and edit first, so each gives a message
with the date to fix. An appointment on the date of birth is allowed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Put the past mark after an appointment's time
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel and export add "(past)" at the end of each past
appointment. A future appointment whose note is "past", or whose WITH
ends in "(past)", ends in the same text, so it looks past too.

Let's put the mark right after the date and time instead. Only the
app writes those, and typed text only comes after them, so nothing a
user types can look like the mark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test editing the DOB of a patient with no appts

appointments, so one branch of it is untested and the coverage check
fails.

Let's test that such a patient's DOB can be edited.

commitResults.messageTitle: Build the past mark from an appointment's parts
commitResults.messageBody:
PatientFormatter splits an appointment's text after its date and time,
with an assert that the text starts with them. The failing side of the
assert can never run, so the coverage check counts it as untested.

Let's have Appointment give its date and time and its other details
as separate texts, which toString joins, so the formatter can put the
mark between them without splitting the text or asserting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat accents typed two ways as the same WITH
commitResults.messageBody:
An accented letter can be stored as one character, e.g. "é", or as a
letter followed by a combining accent. Both look the same, but the
duplicate check for appointments compares them as different text, so
the same appointment can be added twice.

Let's compare WITH in Unicode NFC form, as #373 does for contact
names, so both spellings count as the same. The spelling typed is
still the one saved and shown.
